title: Tingley's problem
description: OpenAI's solution (2026) of Tingley's problem: every surjective isometry between the unit spheres of real normed spaces extends to a surjective real-linear isometry of the whole spaces. The course proves the Mazur–Ulam theorem, makes a hypothetical positive defect attained in an ultrapower, finds aligned extremal chords as a fixed point of a return map with Darbo's theorem (proved from Schauder's and Brouwer's), and rules them out by support, secant and convexity estimates.

units.title: Supports, radial contact and the Mazur–Ulam theorem

prerequisites: foundations-of-von-neumann-algebras lesson hahn-banach-baire-and-the-basic-theorems-on-banach-spaces (Theorem 1.1, Zorn's lemma; Corollary 2.3, Hahn-Banach for normed spaces); lesson weak-topologies-tychonoff-banach-alaoglu-mazur-bipolars-krein-milman-and-eberlein-smulian (Theorem 3.1, only in an exercise)
index-theory-of-elliptic-operators lesson lebesgue-s-covering-theorem-and-the-dimension-of-cubes (Corollary 1.2, Brouwer's theorem for compact convex subsets of R^n, from core course D60)
real analysis: intermediate value theorem, convex functions of one variable, compactness in R^n
